conditions.detail: Three-node DGX Spark cluster: ray head 192.168.1.11 (this box, harness ran here) + workers 192.168.1.2 and 192.168.1.7, one GB10 each, ray 2.57.0. Head node also hosts an idle GNOME session (Xorg + gnome-shell, ~24 MiB VRAM) and earlyoom; no other compute anywhere. Ambient GPU state at start: 48C, 11W.
conditions.isolation_check: Measured, not asserted: nvidia-smi compute apps on the head node at run start = exactly one process (ray::RayWorkerProc, 95,479 MiB). Ray cluster resource report: 3.0/3.0 GPUs reserved by this engine's placement group across all three nodes, so no other GPU work was schedulable cluster-wide; 0B object-store and host memory in use outside the job.

gotchas.text: TP=3 is three GB10 nodes over the cluster fabric (ray head 192.168.1.11 + workers .2/.7), not three GPUs in one box: tensor-parallel all-reduce crosses the network every layer, so per-token latency here is bound by inter-node transfer in a way no single-node GB10 cell is. Compare only against hardware.count=3 cells, and note the recorded nvfp4 arms on this hardware are single-node.

The container is a locally built image, local/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next-tp3-ray2.57.0-r2 (entrypoint 'ray start --head', ray 2.57.0; 'vllm serve' runs as a job inside it), not the upstream vllm/vllm-openai image the 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198 version string suggests.
VLLM_MARLIN_USE_ATOMIC_ADD=1 is set in the image environment (not a CLI flag); it is recorded here because args only carries flags and it plausibly affects MoE marlin kernel selection on sm_121.

Speculative decoding is the model's own trained MTP head at num_speculative_tokens=4 here; the single-node nvfp4 arms on this hardware use 3. Decode throughput is not like-for-like across those cells.

Prefix caching is ON in this arm (--enable-prefix-caching); the earlier GB10 arms disabled it over a GDN kernel bug in their build. serve-chat-c8 samples mostly distinct prompts so the cache is near-inert for this workload, but the flag differs from the other arms. --enforce-eager is also on here (no CUDA graphs), where the nvfp4 arms captured PIECEWISE graphs.
Telemetry (gpu_util/power/temp) is sampled on the head node only - one of the three GPUs; the two worker nodes' sensors are not captured by this result.

provenance.notes: First fp8 arm for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on GB10 and first multi-node cell on this hardware: --tensor-parallel-size 3 with --distributed-executor-backend ray spans three DGX Sparks, one rank per node, so hardware.count=3. Weights are the official Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (revision 970c569, 131 shards, 185.5 GB tensor data per the quant registry) - they cannot fit a single 128 GB GB10, which is the reason for the 3-way shard. Server was already running (attach mode); harness only measured.
